title: A PostgreSQL numeric scale widening lands rounded, with no error, without the DDL support objects

found.by: DDL matrix: PostgreSQL standard CDC reruns with and without DDL support objects

symptom: NUMERIC(10,2) to NUMERIC(18,4) on a standard CDC table: the update completes with no error, the destination keeps decimal(10,2), and 3.1234 lands as 3.12
cause: Without the DDL support objects and inline DDL tracking, the scale change isn't applied to the destination; new values are written at the old scale
effect: Silent loss of precision: no pipeline event, no failed update, the value in the destination differs from the source
fix: Check the destination type after any type change. With the DDL support objects and inline DDL tracking, the same change stops the table with DDL_NOT_SUPPORTED, so it is visible; after a table reset the destination keeps decimal(18,4) and 3.1234
notes: Rerun 2026-10-26, no objects: the update completed. With objects: the table stopped, then a table-only reset loaded 3.1234 at the new scale through the snapshot.
